thread.title: Dow Futures Edge Lower On Italy Weakness; Chevron, Exxon Mobil Slide

author: EdJenner
title: Dow Futures Edge Lower On Italy Weakness; Chevron, Exxon Mobil Slide
text:
Go to Article
Dow futures and other indexes were under modest selling pressure early Monday, weighed down by weakness in European and Asian markets overnight, while FAANG stocks sold off in premarket action.
Futures for the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 showed losses ranging from 0.1% to 0.2% before the opening bell on the stock market today .
Among the FAANG stocks, Netflix ( NFLX ) was down 1.5% in early trading while Google-parent Alphabet ( GOOGL ) gave back 0.8%. Apple ( AAPL ) eased 0.1% while Facebook ( FB ) and Amazon.com ( AMZN ) slipped 0.2% to 0.5%, respectively.
Two of the FAANG stocks, Apple and Amazon, held up relatively well in the latest week despite a Bloomberg report some of their data-center servers might have been compromised by Chinese spy chips .
In overseas markets, the FTSE MIB, the benchmark Italian stock market index, was down 2.4% on growing fears of a budget clash with the European Union about the country’s plans for a wider deficit. Losses in England, Germany and France ranged from 0.7% to 1%.
After a week off, the Shanghai composite crumbled 3.7%. The Hang Seng dipped 1.4%.
IShares MSCI Brazil ( EWZ ) surged 9% to 40.10 in premarket trading. Investor favorite Jair Bolsonaro took a commanding lead in the presidential election .
Brazil-based oil and gas name Petrobras ( PBR ) soared 14% in premarket trading. Dow Futures: Chevron, Exxon Mobil Pace Declines
Chevron ( CVX ), Exxon Mobil ( XOM ) and Boeing ( BA ) were early decliners in the Dow, with losses ranging from 0.6% to 0.8%.
At the New York Mercantile Exchange, U.S. crude oil futures were down more than 1% to $73.34 a barrel.
Third-quarter earnings season starts off this week with some high-profile results due at the end of the week. Results from JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ), Citigroup ( C ) and Wells Fargo ( WFC ) are due Friday before the open.
JPMorgan and Citigroup were looked at as possible call option trades in the latest Earnings Preview column.
The bond market is closed today due to the Columbus Day holiday.
